me.name: Brylie Wilson
me.lede: I’m in my element at the start of a project, working out what the problem actually is.
bio: I research the whole system around a brief, including the people, culture, platforms, social context and politics involved, then translate it into a strategy and something people can see and use. That might be editorial, a campaign, an installation or a digital experience, whichever medium suits the concept best.
I’m drawn to small, values-aligned teams, non-profits, community organisations and civic tech, and to research-led roles where I can keep asking who, what, where, why, and who’s missing.
me.aside: Having too many tabs open is my specialty

copy.brief: A uni assignment for Typography in Context: a magazine for visual communication designers, with masthead, covers and a style guide.
copy.insight: While organising my photographs into sections, I realised there was a cohesive colour scheme that heavily contrasted against the mundane urban landscape surrounding it.
copy.pull: Tags are acts of resistance to the increasing standardisation of urban environments.
copy.response: I colour-graded my photos and masked the backgrounds to enhance this contrast. One spot colour per spread gives the range of street art without clashing, on a grid deliberately broken in key moments, where imposed order coexists with graffiti.

works.context: 2025 · Asterisk Studios, team of 6 · With WAGEC via UTS Shopfront

images.caption: Printed cards. Card questions are by WAGEC. I set the card typography, shared the layout with Rachel, made the majority of the speech-bubble shapes and did the colours, textures and shadows. Teammates made the final artwork.

images.from: 01_UNI/U25-SRD-T2_16-Days-of-Real-Talk/04_Final/FINAL/Final_Deliverables/_Final Deliverables/SOCIAL REELS/ANONYMOUS/Do you think your online experience would be diffe/Do you think your online experience would be diffe-Cover.jpg

copy.brief: A live client project for Socially Responsive Design at UTS. The Women’s and Girls’ Emergency Centre (WAGEC) asked our studio to launch its We Need To Talk cards to university students during the 16 Days of Activism against gender-based violence.
copy.pull: Almost half the students we surveyed had seen or experienced sexism at uni in the past year.
copy.response: We redesigned the deck as 30 pocket-sized cards, colour-coded by topic so students choose how deep to go. We used speech bubbles as the main device to show that not every opinion has to be fully formed to be part of the conversation. I worked on research and positioning, project management and the kickoff workshop, and designed and built the landing page in Webflow.

copy.brief: A university assignment for Visualising Experience at UTS, working with the Powerhouse Museum collection: design an interactive digital experience for one object. I chose Christopher Dresser’s cast-iron Garden Chair, 1870.
copy.insight: We see the chair as either a utilitarian object or a piece of art. Reading Dresser’s own books, I found that division reflects design for standardisation rather than an intrinsic truth, and that his ornament is built on botany and geometry.
copy.pull: Symbiosis is an immersive installation inspired by Dresser’s philosophy that true appreciation of beauty arises from contextual knowledge and understanding.
copy.response: It uses the Garden Chair to critique the arbitrary homogenisation of everyday objects. Visitors enter through mesh pathways with projections on the walls and floor, and symbols around the chair light up the principles hidden in its design.
